'During the internal unrest among the Lombards following the succession of King Aistulf, the nobles of Spoleto, in early 757, elected Alboin as their duke' (Duchy of Spoleto page, reopened 2026-10-25). Aistulf died in December 756 and Desiderius replaced him as king in March 757 (Aistulf page, whose regnal table ends Aistulf's tenure as duke in 756 and names Alboin next). ledger.note: 757: thin, bridging a silence. The strip of the 741 shape above lat 43.6 (16 cells, about 4,000 km2; net 22,755 to 19,694 km2 with Cliopatria's small redraw of the west edge) is absent from Cliopatria's 775 shape. The Donation of Pepin page (opened 2026-10-25) says the treaty of 756 conferred on the pope the territories of Ravenna, 'the Pentapolis (the five cities of Rimini, Pesaro, Fano, Senigallia and Ancona)' and 'the Lombard conquests in the Romagna and in the Duchy of Spoleto and Benevento'; it does not say Spoleto lost the Marche coast, or when, and it dates no later change except Charlemagne's confirmation in 778. Cliopatria's Papal States shape of 757-762 covers 15 of the strip's 16 cells and grows from 12,808 to 21,793 km2 in 757, so the loss is dated to the year the duchy is restored without the strip; the papal-states dossier owes the mirror gain. 776: 'In 776, two years after the fall of Pavia, Spoleto fell likewise to Charlemagne.' The duchy, granted to the Church in 774-776 (infobox), becomes an imperial fief ('imperial fief (776-1201)'); the duke Hildeprand, appointed by the pope at the end of 773, stays in place. Used as a rename because the dossier and the colour continue; the overlord change belongs to the kingdom-of-the-franks and papal-states dossiers.

region.text: Chieti and the strip of the Abruzzo coast, annexed 'to the duchy of Spoleto'

ledger.note: 778: mirror of the duchy-of-benevento ledger (loss 778, confidence 1). Cliopatria's Benevento shape loses about 3,700 km2 (15 cells) between 775 and 778, and Cliopatria's Spoleto shape of 860 (east edge 14.77 E) holds exactly that strip beyond the 775 shape (14 of its 15 cells, and nothing else), so the growth of about 3.7k km2 between the 778-841 and 842-859 keyframes has this event. The Principality of Benevento page (reopened 2026-10-25) lists, in the paragraph on the Frankish invasion of 788, 'small gains, notably the annexation of Chieti to the duchy of Spoleto' and gives no year for it; the Duchy of Spoleto page, reopened the same day, does not mention Chieti. The year 778 is kept to agree with the Benevento dossier; if a page dates the annexation after 788, both dossiers move together. Added after reviewer eu-13-a.
788 or 789: the Lombard duke Hildeprand drops out of the record and Charlemagne appoints the Frank Winigis. Year is the page's 'after 788 or 789'; nothing territorial changes.
842: the infobox dates the duchy's 'resurrection as a Frankish margraviate'; Guy I, a Frank, is recorded as duke in 845. The page does not say what happened between Winigis and 842.
877: Lambert I of Spoleto seizes Rome. '877-878: Lambert seized Rome; the Council of Troyes confirmed his excommunication in 878.' The page gives the span, not the month.

878: Lambert's hold on Rome ends. The page gives no withdrawal; the year is that of the Council of Troyes confirming his excommunication. Reviewer eu-13-a follow-up: the Lambert I of Spoleto page (opened 2026-10-25) says Lambert 'entered Rome' in 877 rather than seizing it, that in March 878 he and Adalbert of Tuscany forced the Romans to acknowledge Carloman and besieged the pope in the Leonine City for thirty days, and that he 'returned his sights to Capua after this Roman episode'; it gives no withdrawal date, so 878 (the end of the Spoleto page's span '877-878') stays at confidence 1, month unknown.

region.text: Lambert's share of the kingdom after the October-November 896 meeting near Pavia: the Kingdom of Italy except the territory between the Adda and the Po, which went to Berengar

ledger.note: 896: Lambert and Berengar partition the kingdom near Pavia. 'Berengar keeping the realm between the Adda and the Po and Lambert the rest.' Lambert was already king (crowned May 891, co-emperor 30 April 892); Cliopatria draws his half as Spoleto from 898 and leaves 896-897 empty, so the Kingdom of Italy dossier should treat 891-898 as Lambert's reign.

15 October 898: Lambert dies, 'killed near Marengo', and 'within days, Berengar had taken Pavia'; the Spoleto page has Lambert II 'killed by count Hugh' in 898. The duke's title passes to Guy IV (Lambert page) or Alberic I of Camerino (Spoleto page, 897); the map stops here with Cliopatria. Reviewer eu-13-a: confidence lowered from 3 to 1: Lambert's death and Berengar's taking of his realm are on the pages, but the duchy itself does not end in 898 ('He was succeeded in Spoleto by Guy IV', Lambert page; Alberic I, Boniface I, Theobald after, Spoleto page); the end year is Cliopatria's.

notes: Cliopatria's Duchy of Spoleto row has 8 shapes (577..586, 741..749, 775..777, 860..865, 875..887 in three, 898). The gaps (587..740, 750..774, 778..859, 866..874, 888..897) are years in which the Lombard or Frankish kingdom, or the Kingdom of Italy, is drawn over the duchy, while the Duchy of Spoleto page shows dukes in office in every one; new keyframes carry the neighbouring Cliopatria shape through each gap at low confidence so the map can draw the duchy as a vassal tint; the pages opened give no boundary, so none of these is a measured shape. The shape growth 577 -> 741 and the northern strip lost by 775 are undated by every page opened (events at confidence 1). The 898 shape is Lambert's realm, not the duchy; Berengar's partner share is Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy 898. Pages disagree: Lambert became duke after Guy's death in 894 (Lambert page) or Guy IV received it (Spoleto page); the duke of 897 is Alberic I (Spoleto page) while the Lambert page has Guy IV succeeding Lambert; the Spoleto page numbers the duke who died in 888 Guy II, the Guy III page numbers him III; Guy III's coronation at Langres is March 888 in the introduction and March 889 in the body. The Spoleto page continues to 1226 and beyond (Alberic I killed 924, Boniface I 922, Theobald 929, Berengar II about 949, Otto I's detaching of Sabina, 967 union with Capua and Benevento under Pandulf, 989 Hugh of Tuscany, 1003 union with Tuscany, 1056 Victor II, 1155 Barbarossa, 1201 Otto IV to the Papal States, 1226 Berthold): none of it is in Cliopatria, so the duchy is not mapped after 898 and a gap-filler could extend this dossier or write a march-of-spoleto dossier. No page gave an infobox area, so the area check could not be made. States and entities needing dossiers: Camerino (the March of Camerino, counterpart of the 883 gain). Region names the gazetteer lacks: Camerino (place; used as Macerata province). The Kingdom of the Lombards page is silent on 776, 787, Hrodgaud and Hildeprand; the Liutprand page is silent on Spoleto; budget was 5 pages and 5 were used. Repairs after review (2026-10-25): the 750-774 keyframe is split into 750 and 757-774, with a loss of the whole duchy to kingdom-of-the-lombards in 751 (Aistulf's direct rule, Aistulf page) and the gain back in 757 (Alboin elected in early 757, Duchy of Spoleto page); the Pentapolis strip above lat 43.6 is a confidence-1 loss to papal-states in 757 (Donation of Pepin page, silent on Spoleto); Chieti and the Abruzzo coast strip are a confidence-1 gain from duchy-of-benevento in 778, mirroring the Benevento ledger (the Principality of Benevento page puts it after 788, undated); the 571 start is kept and the double claim with the Eastern Roman Empire until 577 is stated. The pages disagree on Aistulf's predecessor (Lupus on the Spoleto page, Unnolf in the Aistulf page's table) and on whether a duke Unulf sat in 753 during Aistulf's direct rule. The Faroald II page dates no growth of the duchy, and the Lambert I page does not date Lambert's withdrawal from Rome. Still owed by other dossiers: kingdom-of-the-lombards (loss of Spoleto in 757, and for the 577-741 growth), papal-states (gain of the Pentapolis strip in 757), duchy-of-benevento (the Chieti year), eastern-roman-empire (the 577 hand-over against the 571 start).
